bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services relating to "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Marketplace Integrity and Affordability".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the rule titled Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Marketplace Integrity and Affordability , which was issued by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services on June 25, 2025. The rule makes several changes to enrollment requirements for health insurance exchanges, including (1) requiring annual open enrollment periods for all exchanges to begin by November 1 and end by December 31, (2) requiring all exchanges to conduct pre-enrollment verification of eligibility for at least 75% of new enrollments through special enrollment periods, and (3) prohibiting Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients from enrolling in plans through exchanges or in state Basic Health Programs (state programs for certain low-income residents). The rule also prohibits individual and small group health insurers from covering certain sex-trait modification procedures as an essential health benefit.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution would block a federal rule issued in June 2025 that changes how people enroll in health insurance through the Affordable Care Act marketplaces. The rule sets new enrollment deadlines, requires more identity checks for certain applicants, bars people with DACA status from using the marketplaces, and prevents insurers from covering certain medical procedures as essential benefits. If passed, the resolution would nullify these changes and leave prior rules in place.

industries.rationale: The bill would reverse requirements affecting health insurers' enrollment processes, eligibility verification obligations, and coverage mandates for essential health benefits.
Changes to marketplace enrollment periods and coverage of certain procedures would affect patient volume and reimbursement for hospitals and physician groups.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the rule titled Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Marketplace Integrity and Affordability, which was issued by the agency that runs Medicare and Medicaid on June 25, 2025.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys health insurance. Anyone who pays a medical bill.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what your plan covers. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
